title: Design a Vector Search System for RAG
prompt: Design a vector search system that supports retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): given a query embedding, return the most similar document chunks from a large, continuously growing corpus, fast enough to sit in the critical path of an LLM request.
requirements: Functional: ingest and embed new documents (chunked), support approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings, return top-k results with metadata
Non-functional: corpus in the hundreds of millions of vectors, query latency low enough to not dominate end-to-end LLM response time, index must support ongoing writes without full rebuilds
discussion_points: Approximate nearest-neighbor index choice (e.g. HNSW, IVF) and the recall/latency/memory tradeoffs between them
Sharding the index across machines as the corpus grows, and how a query fans out and merges results
Handling continuous ingestion of new documents without stalling queries or requiring full re-indexing
Filtering by metadata (e.g. only search a specific user's documents) alongside the vector similarity search
Freshness vs. cost tradeoff: how quickly a newly ingested document becomes searchable
How this component fits into the overall RAG request path and what happens if it's slow or down
